title: fastpath eviction coordinator and scaleback recovery for hosted GPU pool collapse
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Follow-up action for a recent hosted API outage where a rapid tenant surge plus a batching admission regression caused GPU pools to exhaust, leading to long queue growth and widespread throttling. This ticket coordinates implementation of a lightweight fastpath eviction coordinator, emergency scaleback and queue-driven admission signals, and associated telemetry and runbook updates so recovery is faster and safer in future events.
context: On 2026-02-04 we observed a hosted API incident: a small percentage of tenants sent high-concurrency short requests which amplified due to a regression in request batching prefilling. The autoscaler did not react quickly due to hysteresis and conservative cooldowns; eviction and preemption took minutes to reclaim slots because of contention between allocator and tenant-level admission. Result: sustained GPU saturation, queue backlog grew >120s median latency for many tenants, automated throttles triggered causing customer-facing errors.
investigation_findings: Regressed batching prefill: a change in continuous-batching heuristics increased prefix cache warming time and kept KV caches pinned, reducing effective throughput for short requests.
Autoscaler hysteresis: scale-up thresholds and cooldowns tuned for steady load failed to respond to flash surges; scale-down logic prevented quick reclaiming until queue drained, creating a deadlock.
Eviction path contention: the existing eviction path requires holding a global allocator lock while draining tenant slots; under load this serialized reclamation and increased latency to free GPUs.
Admission scoring undervalued queue backlog: admission gates relied on token consumption rates and CPU proxies rather than queue length signals, delaying fast-fail and tenant backoff.
Insufficient runbook automation: on-call steps were manual and required multiple service owners to coordinate; this slowed emergency mitigations.
Telemetry gaps: real-time queue-length per pool was noisy and not surfaced on a single incident dashboard, making diagnosis slower.
proposed_solution_overview: Ship a three-part mitigation: 1) Eviction coordinator (fastpath) that can perform lock-free lightweight preemption of opportunistic slots to reclaim capacity within 10s; 2) Queue-driven emergency scale policy that triggers temporary aggressive scale-up/scale-down override based on sustained queue percentiles and request drop rates; 3) Admission signal augmentation to include pool queue-length and per-tenant burst credit decay (smoothing) so small surges don't amplify.
action_items: Design and implement eviction coordinator: create a coordinator service that uses optimistic slot reclamation and per-shard preemption to avoid global allocator lock. Owner: Ravi. Estimate: 5 points. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2142

Add queue-length based autoscale policy: implement a new autoscaler mode 'emergency-queue' that looks at p50/p90 queue length and triggers step-scaling with reduced cooldowns. Owner: Sara Nguyen. Estimate: 3 points. Issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/issues/487
Augment admission gates: include pool-level queue metrics and per-tenant burst credits with decay windows; add backoff jitter to reduce synchronized retries. Owner: Miguel Ortega. Estimate: 3 points.

Improve telemetry and incident dashboard: surface per-pool queue percentiles, eviction latency, and per-tenant admission score. Create an alert on sustained p90 queue > 60s. Owner: Observability team. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/queues/hosted-gpu-pools
Run automated game-day tests: create a chaos scenario simulating 30% of tenants bursting at 10x baseline to validate fastpath coordinator and emergency autoscale. Owner: SRE. Scheduled: 2026-03-15.

Update runbook and automate emergency path: codify steps to enable emergency-queue mode and to toggle preemption aggressiveness; provide CLI shortcuts and a one-click Console control. Owner: Ops Docs. PR: https://drive.redwood.ai/hosted-capacity/runbook-v2
Post-deploy verification and rollout: Canary the eviction coordinator on 10% of pools for 48 hours, monitor tail latency and queue metrics, then escalate rollout. Owner: Release team.
Postmortem writeup and customer comms: prepare a concise incident summary for impacted customers with mitigation timeline and SLA credit guidance. Owner: Incident Response.
Retrospective and follow-ups: schedule a 2-week retro to validate whether kernel selection or quantization interactions contributed. Owner: Research/Applied ML.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial postmortem completed; severity reviewed; action items drafted and prioritized by on-call and platform leads.
2026-02-20: Eviction coordinator design doc reviewed by allocator and SRE; concerns raised about safety and double-free risks; added conservative canary plan.
2026-02-27: Prototype coordinator implemented (lock-free optimistic reclaim) and unit tests added; bench microbench shows 8x faster reclaim in synthetic workload.
2026-03-03: Autoscaler emergency-queue prototype merged into staging branch; simulation harness shows 60% faster capacity recovery under flash loads.
2026-03-05: Telemetry panels created in staging Grafana; alert thresholds proposed and reviewed by on-call.
2026-03-08: Security review confirmed no new data egress risk; evacuation preemption only touches ephemeral tenant slots; security signoff recorded.
2026-03-10: Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-12 to 2026-03-14 on non-critical pools; SLO smoke tests prepared.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction coordinator deployed to canary pools and demonstrates >50% reduction in median reclaim time vs baseline in synthetic bursts.
Emergency-queue autoscale mode triggers within target SLA window (<30s detection, <90s effective scale-up) during replay tests and does not cause oscillation in steady traffic.
Admission gate changes reduce percent of rejected short requests during burst replays by >40% without increasing tail latency post-burst.
Dashboards and alerts are live with documented runbook actions; on-call can enable emergency mode from Console with documented one-click steps.
Post-deploy retro completed with remediation/roll-forward plan and customer-facing incident summary published.
notes: This ticket focuses on recovery speed and safety. Longer-term capacity optimizations (packing, quantization tuning) will be tracked in a separate epic. Coordinate closely with Autoscaler, Allocator, and Observability owners to avoid overlapping rate-limit changes during canary windows.
